summary: The root سغب (sgb) primarily means to be hungry. It can also imply hunger combined with fatigue.
lane: 1 سَغِبَ ذ , aor. سَغَبَ ; (S A, Msb, K;) and سَغَبَ , aor. سَغُبَ ; (A, K;) inf. n. سَغَبٌ , (S, A, * Msb, K,) which is of the former, (Sudot;, Msb, TA,) and سَغْبٌ , (K,) which is of the latter, (TA,) and سُغُوبٌ (K) and سَغَابَةٌ and مَسْغَبَةٌ , (A, * K,) the last syn. with مَجَاعَةٌ ; (S, Msb;) He was, or became, hungry: (S, A, Msb, K:) or suffered hunger together with fatigue. (A, Msb, K.) You say, بِهِ سَغَبٌ and مَسْغَبَةٌ and سَغَابَةٌ , [using these ns. as simple substs.,] In him is hunger: or hunger together with fatigue. (A.) And يَتِيمٌ ذُو مَسْغَبَةٍ [ An orphan ] having hunger. (S.) And فِى يَوْمٍ ذِى مَسْغَبَةٍ , in the Kur [xc. 14], means In a day of hunger. (TA.) [See also سَغْبَةٌ and سَغَبٌ below.]
